raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #46495.

With `max_tokens` unset (the OpenAI chat default), `max_new_tokens` is about the context length minus the prompt. After a KV-full retraction the scheduler sets the new-token ratio to `retract_decode`'s estimate, which divides by the survivors' unclipped `max_new_tokens` (`new_token_ratio_tracker.py:41-49`). So it lands far below `NewTokenRatioTracker.min`, which every other writer of the ratio (init, `decay_step`, `reset`) keeps. Admission multiplies the ratio by each running request's remainder clipped to 4096 (`schedule_policy.py:756-765`). So right after the pool ran out it reserves much less decode headroom and admits more prefill work, until the next decode step puts the ratio back at the floor.

The issue has the CPU repro and its output on main: the ratio goes 0.0980 -> 0.0117, the survivors' decode reservation drops from 15254 to 1819 tokens, and two fresh 2000-token requests are admitted with 20000 tokens free (none at the floor).

## Modifications

`update_running_batch` clamps the estimate to the tracker's floor (`scheduler.py:4471`, one line plus a comment). Above the floor the estimate is used as before: with `max_tokens=2048` it is 0.7422, and a later retraction can still lower the ratio toward the floor.

The issue lists two other forms: the estimate in clipped units, or on the clipped remainder. Both change the estimate itself, and `add_one_req_ignore_eos` (`schedule_policy.py:1217-1223`) multiplies the ratio by unclipped `max_new_tokens`: with `max_tokens` unset either would reserve about 47k tokens per running request there, against about 11k at the floor. The issue also mentions clamping to the current ratio, which would keep a ratio that an earlier retraction raised. I kept to the floor. I'll switch to another form if you prefer it.

The retraction warning now logs the applied ratio, so a clamped retraction logs `0.0980 -> 0.0980`.

## Accuracy Tests

New file `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_retract_ratio.py`, like the other `test_scheduler_*.py` files there: it needs its own fixture, a bare `Scheduler` with a real `NewTokenRatioTracker` and a stubbed batch. It drives the real `update_running_batch`.

- `max_tokens` unset, ratio at 0.5: the retraction sets the floor, not the estimate and not the old ratio.
- `max_tokens=2048`: the retraction still raises the ratio to the estimate.

`test_scheduler_pause_generation.py` gets one line: its stub tracker gains `min`.

On CPU:

- main: 1 failed, 1 passed (`AssertionError: 0.011686012858255906 != 0.098`)
- this PR: 2 passed; `test_retraction_order.py`, `test_scheduler_pause_generation.py`, `test_scheduler_flush_cache_after_retract.py` and `test_schedule_policy.py` still pass (47 passed, 10 subtests), as do four more scheduler test files that stub `update_running_batch` or the tracker (26 passed, 56 subtests)

Not run: a GPU job.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: one `max` per retraction. Right after a below-floor retraction admission reserves what it reserves at the floor, as on every other step; I have not measured throughput under KV pressure.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not run (CPU only; see Speed Tests).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Developed with AI assistance (Claude); every changed line was reviewed and the tests were run locally by me.

@@ -4815,6 +4815,9 @@ def update_running_batch(self, batch: ScheduleBatch) -> Optional[ScheduleBatch]:
                 else None
             )
             retracted_reqs, new_token_ratio, reqs_to_abort = batch.retract_decode()
+            # Unclipped max_new_tokens can put the estimate below the floor;
+            # keep the floor that decay_step and reset also keep.
+            new_token_ratio = max(new_token_ratio, self.new_token_ratio_tracker.min)
             self.running_reqs.leave([*retracted_reqs, *reqs_to_abort])
             new_available_tokens = self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.available_size()
             new_token_gained = new_available_tokens - old_available_tokens

@@ -276,7 +276,7 @@ def _retract_by_kv_full(self, scheduler: Scheduler, req: Req):
         scheduler.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.page_size = 1
         scheduler.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.check_decode_capacity.return_value = False
         scheduler.tree_cache.req_to_token_pool.mamba_allocator = None
-        scheduler.new_token_ratio_tracker = SimpleNamespace(current=1.0)
+        scheduler.new_token_ratio_tracker = SimpleNamespace(current=1.0, min=0.0)
         scheduler.ipc_channels = MagicMock()
         scheduler.rust_server = None
         scheduler.output_streamer = MagicMock()

@@ -0,0 +1,74 @@
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler import Scheduler
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler_components.new_token_ratio_tracker import (
+    NewTokenRatioTracker,
+)
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler_components.running_reqs import RunningReqs
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+FLOOR = 0.098
+
+
+def _survivors(n: int, output_len: int, max_new_tokens: int):
+    return [
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            output_ids=[0] * output_len,
+            sampling_params=SimpleNamespace(max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens),
+        )
+        for _ in range(n)
+    ]
+
+
+def _ratio_after_kv_full_retract(survivors, current: float) -> float:
+    scheduler = Scheduler.__new__(Scheduler)
+    scheduler.enable_skip_finishing_decode = False
+    scheduler.result_queue = []
+    scheduler.decode_offload_manager = None
+    scheduler.token_to_kv_pool_allocator = MagicMock()
+    scheduler.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.available_size.return_value = 0
+    scheduler.tree_cache = MagicMock()
+    scheduler.tree_cache.req_to_token_pool.mamba_allocator = None
+    scheduler.metrics_reporter = MagicMock(enable_metrics=False)
+    scheduler._add_request_to_queue = MagicMock()
+    scheduler.running_reqs = RunningReqs()
+    scheduler.new_token_ratio_tracker = NewTokenRatioTracker(
+        init=0.7, min=FLOOR, decay=0.001, current=current
+    )
+
+    batch = MagicMock()
+    batch.is_empty.return_value = False
+    batch.batch_size.return_value = len(survivors)
+    batch.check_decode_mem.return_value = False
+    estimate = NewTokenRatioTracker.estimate_new_token_ratio_after_retract(survivors)
+    batch.retract_decode.return_value = ([MagicMock()], estimate, [])
+
+    scheduler.update_running_batch(batch)
+    return scheduler.new_token_ratio_tracker.current
+
+
+class TestKvFullRetractNewTokenRatio(CustomTestCase):
+    """A KV-full retraction must not set the new-token ratio below its floor,
+    even when the survivors' max_new_tokens is close to the context length."""
+
+    def test_unset_max_tokens_stops_at_the_floor(self):
+        # max_tokens unset: max_new_tokens is about context minus prompt.
+        survivors = _survivors(38, output_len=1500, max_new_tokens=130070)
+        self.assertEqual(_ratio_after_kv_full_retract(survivors, current=0.5), FLOOR)
+
+    def test_a_higher_estimate_still_raises_the_ratio(self):
+        survivors = _survivors(38, output_len=1500, max_new_tokens=2048)
+        ratio = _ratio_after_kv_full_retract(survivors, current=FLOOR)
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(ratio, (1500 + 20) / 2048, places=3)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
